input.quote: ARTICLE XII INDEMNITY Licensee will be solely responsible for any commercial or legal liability that may arise as a result of Licensee's exercise of any of the license rights granted by Licensor to Licensee under this Agreement, and Licensee shall defend, indemnify, and hold Licensor harmless from and against any and all suits, claims, proceedings, judgments, awards, damages, loss, liability, cost and expenses (including without limitation reasonable attorney's fees and other related costs) that are incurred or suffered by Licensor or any of its affiliates, directors, officers, employees, or agents
input.rationale: Article XII (p0128-p0129) is a one-way indemnity running from Licensee (us) to Licensor covering our exercise of the license, the conduct of our business and any breach by us. There is no Licensor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement, and Article XIII (p0130) compounds the problem by stating that "UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE FOR ANY ACTIONS, CLAIMS OR THE LIKE ... THAT THE USE OF THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY HAS RESULTED ... IN ANY INFRINGEMENT ... OF THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY ... RIGHTS OF ANY PERSON", while the warranty disclaimer excludes non-infringement. That is the rule's walk-away scenario (no Vendor IP indemnity at all, plus a one-way Customer indemnity for the Vendor's technology), so it fails the fallback on a material term. Our redline inserts the preferred Licensor defence/indemnity for third-party IP, breach of law, data-breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct claims with standard notice-control-cooperation mechanics, carves it out of the Article XIII exclusions so it is not rendered illusory, and narrows our indemnity to Licensee-provided content and our own breach of law. The fallback (usual IP exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, with a 3x fees super-cap) is offered in the comment as a landing zone.

proposal.summary: Add Licensor IP/misconduct indemnity in Article XII and narrow the Licensee indemnity to Licensee content and breach of law
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XII currently runs one way only, and Article XIII expressly disclaims any Licensor liability for infringement claims, so we have no protection if the Licensed Technology infringes a third party's rights. We have added a reciprocal Licensor defence and indemnity for third-party IP, breach of law, data-breach and wilful misconduct claims (with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics) and narrowed our indemnity to Licensee-provided content and our own breach of law; we can discuss usual IP exclusions (our modifications, combinations and specifications) and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies if helpful.
